summary: Russian forces launched multiple Shahed drone and missile attacks across Ukraine overnight, targeting energy infrastructure and civilian areas. Ukrainian forces reported destroying 2,250 Russian troops, three tanks, 44 artillery systems, eight armored vehicles, 1,750 drones, and 365 vehicles and special equipment in the past 24 hours. Ukraine and Finland signed approximately €300 million in military support agreements.
key_points: Russian attacks targeted energy infrastructure in Rovno with 7-9 Geran-5 missiles (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77423).
Ukrainian forces destroyed 2,250 Russian troops, three tanks, 44 artillery systems, eight armored vehicles, 1,750 drones, and 365 vehicles in 24 hours (Source: @UkraineNow/84833).
Ukraine and Finland signed approximately €300 million in military support agreements (Source: @UkraineNow/84848).
Seven to nine Geran-5 missiles targeted Rovno energy infrastructure (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77423).
Drone attack on market in Lozova on Kharkiv region killed two people and injured 34 (Source: @UkraineNow/84840).
Shahed drone struck residential building in Zhytomyr region, injuring nine people including two children (Source: @UkraineNow/84846).
Ukrainian drones attacked '75th Arsenal' facility in Serpukhov, Moscow region where military equipment is repaired and stored (Source: @UkraineNow/84832).

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces are escalating their campaign of terror attacks against Ukrainian civilian infrastructure and population centers. The coordinated missile and drone attacks targeting energy infrastructure across multiple regions indicate a strategic effort to degrade Ukraine's resilience and force reliance on external support. Ukrainian forces have demonstrated significant capability to destroy Russian air defense systems and military assets deep inside Russian territory, suggesting potential for continued cross-border operations. The intensity and geographic spread of attacks suggest preparation for larger offensive operations in the coming weeks.
sections.regional_response: International support for Ukraine continues to expand with Finland joining other European nations in providing approximately €300 million in military assistance. NATO has facilitated streamlined procurement mechanisms allowing Ukraine to acquire weapons and ammunition more efficiently through the NATO Support and Procurement Agency. Denmark announced $112.6 million credit guarantee for Ukrainian rocket and drone manufacturer Fire Point. These developments indicate growing international commitment despite deteriorating US-Ukraine relations under the Trump administration. The UK has announced plans to strengthen penalties for damage to underwater cables and implement new requirements for operators.
sections.intelligence_notes: Russian naval fishing vessels suspected of conducting reconnaissance of underwater cables near the UK, with over 500 documented incidents involving Russian trawlers tracking communication cable routes between the UK, Europe, and US. NATO is monitoring these civilian vessels for potential intelligence gathering activities. Russian forces appear to be employing a coordinated strategy of simultaneous attacks across multiple fronts to overwhelm Ukrainian defenses and infrastructure. The targeting of railway infrastructure in Poltava region suggests efforts to disrupt logistics and civilian mobility. Ukrainian forces have demonstrated capability to strike high-value targets deep inside Russian territory, including military repair facilities and ammunition storage sites.
